get.summary:
Who the site thinks is calling: their name, whether they are signed in,
whether they are a server administrator, and whether the site has
accounts at all. With an API token, also the token's id, name, grants and
expiry.

The server is up, and the Ridal version it runs. Never requires a login,
so a client can check what it is talking to before signing in.

The OpenAPI description of this API, the same file as the documentation
site's `openapi.json`. Never requires a login: it describes the code,
which is public, and nothing about the site.

The projects the caller is a member of; every project for a server
administrator. Public projects are not listed. With an API token, only its
granted projects, with the role and download scope the token has there.

a consensus computed over other people's picks is the one thing a picker
must not see mid-experiment: seeing it would tell them what everyone else
concluded, which is exactly the bias the study design exists to avoid.

about what a given viewer gets: the same project-wide definition yields the
full consensus for an operator and a personal result for a picker. That is
what lets a consensus be defined and monitored while picking is still open.

On by default. An intermediate layer -- one that exists only as an

along the radargram.

Users whose picks could not be carried onto the current revision and

How far the carried coordinates moved, in index units.

Traces and samples rather than metres or nanoseconds, because that is
what the viewer draws in and what "did this pick move" means on screen.
The median says whether the revisions broadly agree; the worst says
whether any single vertex went somewhere else, which an average would
hide behind a thousand that did not.

Always stored canonically as an array (SPEC §4.1), even when the

The carry that *would* be shown after the replace. Not applied —

Stable and machine-readable, such as `dataset_not_found`. A client
branches on this rather than on `message`.

ExclusivityGroup.description:
A set of layers that cannot all hold a value for one user at one position
(#208).

Membership is deliberately *not* transitive: in the Svalbard setup `bed`
and `bed_no_temperate` are exclusive, and `bed_no_temperate` and
`temperate_ice` are exclusive, but `bed` and `temperate_ice` coexist. Two
layers conflict iff they share at least one group.

id.description: Stable id. A layer may list it in [`Layer::groups`].

members.description: The layers that are mutually exclusive within this group.

additionalProperties.description: Anything a future version adds, preserved on rewrite.

background.description: Background colour as `#rrggbb`, or `null` for transparent.

FigureDerived.description:
Which derived layers to draw, and how.

`items` are derived item ids. Each is drawn in its own colour, and an
item whose range fill reaches another drawn item has the fill drawn
under them, as in the viewer. Only items of kind `layer` are positions
that can be drawn; an attribute is refused.

fills.description: Whether to draw range fills between drawn items.

FigureExtent.description:
The part of the radargram a figure shows, in raster coordinates.

Positions are fractional trace and row indices, the same coordinates
the viewer uses: trace `t` spans `[t, t + 1)` and row `r` spans
`[r, r + 1)`, so `traces: [0, n]` is every trace. In the standard view a
row is a sample. In the topographic view it is a row of the corrected
raster, which moves when the radargram's elevation window is edited, so
a spec meant to outlive that can give `elevation` instead.

Omitted bounds mean the whole radargram. Bounds past the data are
clipped to it, except the rows of the topographic view, which may reach
above the highest surface or below the floor to leave empty space there.

elevation.description:
`[top, bottom]` elevation in metres; topographic view only, and not
together with `rows`.

FigurePicks.description:
Which picked lines to draw, and how.

Every pick whose user and layer match one of `items` is drawn, in its
layer's colour. A selector that leaves out `user` matches everyone whose
picks the caller may see, and one that leaves out `layer` matches every
layer, so `[{}]` is all of them; `"layer": ""` matches unlabelled lines.
No items, the default, draws none.

FigureSidecar.description:
What a figure without axes needs beside it to be plotted elsewhere:
the extent it shows, and each axis's value at every pixel's centre.

In matplotlib, `imshow(img, extent=[*x.extent, *y.extent[::-1]])` for
an axis that is linear, or `pcolormesh` with the centres for one that is
not (distance on a profile driven at varying speed).

rows.description: `[top, bottom]` row position of the top and bottom edges.

extent.description: The value at the two edges: left and right, or top and bottom.

centres.description: The value at the centre of each pixel column or row.

FigureSize.description:
How big the figure is.

`width` is the whole figure's, margins included; the height follows
from the extent and `x_scale`. With `axes: false` there are no margins
and `width` is the radargram's own.

dpi.description:
Pixels per inch. Converts `cm` and `in` to pixels, and point sizes
(fonts, lines) to pixels in every unit.

view.description: The standard or the topographically corrected view.

revision_id.description:
When set, the revision the spec was made for. Rendering it from a
different revision is refused: a reprocessed file can have a
different number of traces, and the same trace numbers would then
show a different stretch of the profile.

profile.description:
A render profile name (built-in, or a file path on the command
line).

x_scale.description:
Horizontal stretch, as the viewer's horizontal scale: the plot is
`traces * x_scale` units wide for every `rows` units tall.

`false` writes the radargram alone, with no axes or margins, plus a

radargram.description:
`false` leaves the radargram out, so only the picks and derived
layers are drawn, over the background.

picks.description: Picked lines to draw over the radargram.

derived.description: Derived layers to draw over the radargram.

The revision the axes describe. A document carrying them should name

oneOf.description:
The `coordinates.axes` block for a gprinterp document (its SPEC
§7.4), or `null` when the file cannot describe its axes.

The highest role the token acts with here. The account's membership
still applies, so the token never has more than the account.

download.description: The widest download scope the token has here, under the same rule.

GroupChoice.description: A group that can be chosen.

GroupMaps.description: `true` shows every group's map, `false` none, and `"listed"` only those of groups with a listed radargram.

`GET /api/v1/groups/{group}/properties`: the project's override of a

What it would show without the override: the name resolved from the

How many radargrams are in it, so the dialog can say what a rename

One radargram's track in `GET /api/v1/groups/{group}/tracks`, keyed by

One heartbeat's numbers, separate from how they are written so a test

(#391).

What the render permits in use are doing, longest-running first

Images in the in-memory render cache, their size in MB, and

Lookups that found their image, since the last heartbeat. `None`

Ignore decisions with nothing to act on, because the radargram is

`true` when these are everyone's interpretations, `false` when only

From starting to ending, or to now while it runs. `None` for a job

A job as a server administrator sees it (#391): its status, the project

Every step has run and the file is being written, which for a long
radargram takes a while of its own.

writing.description: Every step has run and the file is being written.

JobStatusView.description:
[`JobStatus`] without what is the server's business: where its files
are, and the key it was queued under.

Kind.description:
What an expression's value means (#205).

Two kinds, not three. An earlier `Length`/`Scalar` split was never acted on
by any branch — the only decisions are "is it a layer" — and the stored
`unit` already distinguishes a thickness from a count, so the extra terms
only reached the UI and confused it. A **Layer** is a drawable position; an
**Attribute** is a number per position (a length, a count, a spread).

name.description: Display name. Cosmetic; safe to change at any time.

color.description: CSS colour used to draw the layer in the viewer.

allow_overhangs.description:
Permit lines in this layer to double back in trace.

Off by default, because a reflector has one depth per position and a
line that overhangs is usually a mis-click. Some layers legitimately
do overhang -- a crevasse wall, a water-body outline -- which is why
it is a property of the layer rather than of Ridal.

Turning it on has a cost: such a layer cannot be exported at even
spacing along the ground track, because that works by asking the line
for its depth at a position, which is the question an overhang has
two answers to. It exports as its own picked vertices instead. See
[`crate::interp::checks`].

oneOf.description:
How to collapse several picked values for one user at one position to
one. `None` inherits [`LayerSet::default_reducer`].

Reducers apply at **evaluation time only**: stored picks are never
rewritten, so changing a reducer is non-destructive and reversible.

warn_on_duplicates.description:
Whether more than one value for this layer at one trace is worth
pointing out.

Off for a layer that is legitimately multi-valued -- folded englacial
reflectors, say -- where a duplicate is the point rather than a
mistake.

groups.description:
Ids of the exclusivity groups this layer belongs to (#208).

Membership is defined by [`ExclusivityGroup::members`]; this list is
the same relation seen from the layer, and the two are unioned when
conflicts are computed.

additionalProperties.description: Anything a future version adds, preserved on rewrite.

PreferencesBody.description:

alone, `null` clears it -- which is what "Project default" in the
dropdown means -- and a value sets it.

x_scale.description: Horizontal stretch, one of the factors the viewer offers.

show_picks.description: Whether the viewer opens with the interpretations drawn (#143).

basemap.description: Which basemap the maps draw on, by id (#177).

level2_spacing.description: The point spacing the layer-point download dialogs open on (#166).

show_group_radargrams.description:
Whether the catalog opens with each group's radargrams listed
(#314). `null` defers to the project.

oneOf.description:
Which groups' maps the catalog opens with shown (#447). `null`
defers to the project.

open_zoomed_out.description: Whether the viewer opens on the whole radargram (#315).

show_vertex_tooltips.description:
Whether the handles of a line being edited carry their tooltips
(#363).

values.description: One value per position, `null` where there is none.

contributors.description: How many people's picks went into it.

unknown_users.description: Users the expression names whose picks it did not have.

not_carried.description:
Users whose picks could not be carried onto the current revision and
were used as stored.

PreviewBody.description:
The body of `POST /api/v1/datasets/{radargram_id}/derived/preview`: an
expression, evaluated over the caller's picks as a saved item would be.

oneOf.description: The unit it is written in. Default: metres.

Priority.description: Which jobs go first. Declared in that order.

ProcessingLimits.description: The processing limits the server was started with.

snapshot.description: How many jobs are queued and running, and the memory they use.

jobs.description: Every job the queue still knows of.

oneOf.description: Processed as the profile says now, from the raw data its source names.
Processed some other way than the profile and source say now.

profile_version.description: The profile version it was processed with, when it matches one.

custom.description:
Processed with steps or a velocity that match no version of the
profile: changed for this radargram, as opposed to left behind
by the profile. False for a file that records no recipe, which
cannot say.

oneOf.description:
Processed as the profile says, but by an older version of a step or
of the rest of Ridal (#383). Not stale: the same request gives a
different file only because Ridal has changed since.
Raw data and a profile, but nothing processed yet.

No raw data in the project, so nothing can be reprocessed. Never
counted as stale (#382).

Ignored in this project (#409). It keeps its profile, because
lifting the ignore brings it back; until then it is never counted
as stale or not processed, and never taken by a batch.

ProcessingState.description: Where a radargram stands against its processing profile.

versions.description: Oldest first; the last is current. Never empty.

ProfileEdit.description:
The body of `PUT /api/v1/processing/profiles/{profile}`: a processing
profile, created or changed.

steps.description: The processing steps, as `ridal process --steps` takes them.

version.description: From 1, one more for every change to the steps or the velocity.

steps.description:
Canonical, with every argument written out, as a recipe records
them; so a changed default is not a silent change to the profile.

current_version.description: The version radargrams are processed with now.

ProfileView.description: A profile, as the list and the single view give it.

ProjectEntry.description:
One project as the caller sees it: an entry of `GET /api/v1/projects`,
and the whole of `GET /api/v1/projects/{key}`.

key.description:
What the project is addressed by, in `/api/v1/projects/{key}/…`.
`ridal gui` serves its one project as `default`.

name.description: The display name, or the key when the project has none.

description_long_html.description:
The long description rendered from Markdown to HTML, with raw HTML
in the source escaped. `null` when there is none.

created_by.description:
The account that created the project, if it was created through the
site rather than on the command line.

member.description:
Whether the caller is a member, or a server administrator, who is
treated as one.

radargram_count.description:
How many radargrams the last scan found, or `null` if the project
has never been scanned.

role.description:
The caller's role here. A non-member gets `viewer`, and a server
administrator `admin`.

require_auth_to_read.description: Whether reading the project needs a login.

projects.description: The projects the caller may see, in key order.

ProjectSettings.description:
`GET /api/v1/settings`: the project's defaults, what the caller may change,
and the caller's own preferences, for the settings page.

On a server without a project, `project` is `false` and the
project's values are `null`.

project.description: Whether the server is serving a project at all.

can_edit_project.description: Whether the caller may change the project's defaults (`operator`).

can_edit_access.description:
Whether the caller may change members and the access policy: an
`admin`, in a project served by a site.

can_administer.description:
Whether the caller may change what only an `admin` may: the size
limit and the descriptions.

size_bytes.description: The project's size on disk, in bytes. `null` below `operator`.

max_bytes.description: The project's upload size limit, in bytes. `null` below `operator`.

default_max_bytes.description: The limit a project has when it sets none, in bytes.

user.description: The caller's account, or `null` for an anonymous reader.

authentication_configured.description: Whether the site has accounts to sign in to.

root.description: The project directory on the server.

default_profile.description: The render profile a request that names none gets.

processing_crs.description:
The CRS a radargram whose raw data names none is processed in;
`null` for the UTM zone that suits each track.

profiles.description:
The render profiles to choose from, by name: the built-ins that are
not hidden, then the project's own (#183).

hidden_profiles.description: The built-in render profiles this project does not offer.

personal_profiles.description: Whether people may keep render profiles of their own.

default_xscale.description: The horizontal stretch radargrams open at.

xscales.description: The stretch factors the viewer offers.

my_show_picks.description: The caller's own choice of opening the viewer with picks shown.

my_spacing.description: The caller's own point spacing for downloads.

spacings.description: The point spacings the download dialogs offer.

formats.description: The formats the download dialogs offer.

default_spacing.description: The project's point spacing for downloads.

default_show_group_radargrams.description: Whether the catalog opens with each group's radargrams listed.

my_show_group_radargrams.description: The caller's own choice of the same.

my_open_zoomed_out.description: The caller's own choice of opening the viewer zoomed out.

my_show_vertex_tooltips.description: The caller's own choice of tooltips on the handles of a line.

basemaps.description:
The basemaps that may be chosen: the project's own and the built-in
one, without those that cannot be drawn.

project_basemaps.description: The project's own basemaps, as `ridal.toml` holds them.

default_basemap.description: The basemap someone who has not chosen sees; `null` for the first.

built_in_basemap.description: Whether Ridal's built-in basemap is offered.

basemap_problems.description: What is wrong with the project's basemaps that cannot be drawn.

overlays.description: The project's vector overlays, as `ridal.toml` holds them.

overlay_problems.description: What is wrong with the overlays that cannot be drawn.

oneOf.description: Which groups' maps the catalog opens with shown.
The caller's own choice of the same.

Promoted.description:
`POST …/interpretations/{user}/promote`: the carried view is now the
interpretation.

from_revision.description: The revision the picks were drawn on, where the document said.

to_revision.description: The revision they are now drawn on.

dropped.description: Features that did not fit on the new revision and were left out.

archived.description:
Where the interpretation as it was drawn was kept, or `null` when
nothing needed keeping.

Properties.description:
`GET /api/v1/datasets/{radargram_id}/properties`: the project's overrides
of a radargram's metadata, and what each field would be without them.

from_file.description:
What it would show with the override removed, field by field, so
"revert" can be labelled with the value it would revert *to* rather
than being a leap of faith.

overridden.description:
Whether each field is currently overridden, so the dialog can say
which values are the project's opinion and which are the file's.

groups.description:
Every group the catalog knows about, for choosing among them
without having to retype a name and hope the slug matches.

PropertiesBody.description:
The body of `PUT /api/v1/datasets/{radargram_id}/properties`: the whole
override, replaced rather than patched. A field left out is cleared.

display_name.description: `null` or empty reverts to the file's display name.

group_id.description: The group to join, when `grouping` is `group`.

group_name.description:
What that group is called. Stored against the group, not the
radargram, so renaming it is one edit and its members cannot come to
disagree. Omitted leaves any existing name alone.

unlisted.description: Whether to leave it out of the listing for everyone below `operator`.

elevation_min.description: `null` on either side reverts that bound to no range at all (#168).

x_scale.description:
One of the offered scales, or `null` to inherit the user's or the
project's (#411).

QueueSnapshot.description: Counts for a heartbeat or a status page.

RadargramStatus.description: One radargram in a profile, and where it stands.

RawSource.description: What one radargram is made from.

bundles.description: The raw recordings, in the order they are merged.

crs.description: The CRS to project positions into; the project's default otherwise.

oneOf.description: The project's DEM to take elevations from.

antenna_mhz.description:
The antenna's frequency in MHz, where the files do not say it or say
it wrongly; `None` reads it from the files (#409). It describes the
recording, as the CRS and DEM do, so every draft and batch made from
the source uses it.

antenna_separation.description:
The distance between the antennas in m, likewise; `None` reads it
from the files.

oneOf.description:
What to call the radargram while it has none of its own: an id
with raw data and no processed file yet (#382 phase 7). Once it is
served, the catalog's names win and renaming is an override.

RecordingFiles.description: One recording as the request names it.

files.description: The files it is made of, as `POST /api/v1/raw` answered.

token.description: The one-time token from the invite link.

Reducer.description:
How to collapse several picked values for one user at one position into
one, at evaluation time (#207).

`Shallowest` is the project default: stray picks on multiples and ringing
lie *below* the true reflector, so the minimum depth is the defensible
choice.

invite_path.description: The invite link's path, `/invite/<token>`. It is shown this once.

invite_expires.description: When it expires, in Unix seconds.

outcome.description:
`removed` when the file was deleted, `ignored` when it lives in a
read-only root and was only dropped from the catalog.

archived.description:
How many interpretations were archived. Zero is worth reporting: it
is the difference between "nobody had picked this" and "your picks
are somewhere".

RenderKind.description: What a render permit is being used for.

view.description: Which vertical arrangement of the radargram it draws.

source_transform.description:
Applied to each sample before anything is resampled. Unset is
`None`.

siglog_minval_log10.description:
The strength of a `SigLog` source transform: the log10 magnitude
below which samples truncate to zero. Only for `SigLog`; unset is
the `siglog` processing step's default.

siglog_noise_offset.description:
The offset of an `AdaptiveSigLog` source transform from the
radargram's noise floor, in log10 units: the strength is
`log10(noise) + offset`. Only for `AdaptiveSigLog`; unset is the
`adaptive_siglog` processing step's default.

transform.description:
How a resampled value is mapped before it is stretched between the
limits.

limits.description: The amplitudes that map to the two ends of the scale.

resampling.description:
How samples are combined where a pixel covers several (tiles only;
overviews and figures average colours).

contrast.description:
Multiplies the stretched value, after `black_level` is subtracted.
`1` leaves the stretch between the limits as it is.

black_level.description:
Subtracted from the stretched value (0 to 1) before `contrast`. `0`
leaves the stretch as it is.

oneOf.description:
A colour scale. Unset is grey, from black at the low limit to white
at the high one.

symmetric_limits.description:
Make the limits symmetric about zero, `(-max, max)` with the larger
of the two magnitudes, so that a diverging colour scale's middle is
zero amplitude. Unset is `false`.

stats_skip_first_samples.description:
Samples left out at the top of every trace when estimating
percentile limits, to keep the direct wave out of the estimate.

nodata_color.description:
The colour, as `[red, green, blue]` from 0 to 255, of a tile or
overview pixel with no data under it. Unset is mid-grey. Figures
leave such pixels transparent instead.

profiles.description: Built-ins first, then the project's own, hidden ones included.

default.description:
The profile a request that names none renders with: the project's
default, or `default`.

hidden.description:
Left out of the lists people choose from, but still rendered when
asked for by name. Only a built-in can be hidden.

thumbnail_profile.description:
For a personal profile, the shared profile the catalog's thumbnails
are drawn with while it is chosen; unset is the project's default.
`null` for every other profile.

RenderProfileView.description: A render profile, as the list and the single view give it.

include_older.description:
Also reprocess what an older Ridal processed exactly as the profile
says (`older_processing`). Off by default: that is not stale.

radargram_ids.description:
Only these of the profile's radargrams, such as one catalog group's.
Omitted, every one.

ResamplingMethod.description: How a tile combines the samples a pixel covers.

RestoredInterpretation.description:
`POST …/archived/{radargram_id}/{removal}/{user}/restore`: the
interpretation is back on its radargram.

removal.description: The archive entry it came from.

revision_id.description: The revision the document says it was drawn on, if it says.

current.description:
Whether that is the revision the catalog serves now. When it is not,
the picks are carried onto it like any other stale interpretation,
and their owner adopts them as usual.

version.description: The restored document's version, as sent in `ETag`.

RevisionDeclarations.description:
A processed file's identity and axis declarations: everything a
replace's consequence report reads from the incoming file (#331).

The body of `POST /api/v1/datasets/{radargram_id}/replace/preflight`,
and what `ridal._ridal._preflight_body` reads from a local file for the
Python client (#328), so one type is both ends of the request. A type of
its own rather than [`AxisDeclarations`] itself, so the API does not
change when that internal type does.

radargram_id.description: The file's radargram id. It must be the radargram in the path.

processing_datetime.description:
The file's `ridal_processing_datetime` attribute, verbatim. With the
radargram id it gives the revision id of a file without a recipe.

recipe_hash.description:
The file's `ridal_recipe_hash` attribute (#382), or `null` when it
has none. When present, it and the radargram id give the revision
id instead of the datetime.

time.description:
The file's `time` variable: acquisition time per trace, in seconds
since the Unix epoch.

twtt_anchor.description:
The `anchor_name` attribute of the file's `twtt` variable, or `null`
when it has none.

twtt_crop.description:
The file's `twtt_crop` variable: one value, one per trace, or empty
when the file has none.

twtt_time_zero.description: The file's `twtt_time_zero` variable, in the same way.

dt_ns.description:
The spacing of the file's `twtt` variable in nanoseconds (its second
value minus its first), or 0 when it has fewer than two.

n_samples.description: The length of the file's `twtt` variable.

antenna_separation_effective_m.description:
The file's `antenna_separation_effective` attribute, in metres:
zero once the radargram was corrected for the separation.

logged_resolution_m.description:
The depth grid spacing in metres that the file's `processing_log`
records for `correct_antenna_separation`, when it records one.

RevisionSummary.description: One revision a radargram has been through.

current.description: Whether it is the one currently behind the id.

superseded_at.description: When it stopped being current, RFC 3339.

has_axes.description:
Whether this revision's axes were kept, which is what decides
whether picks drawn on it can be carried onto a later one.

n_traces.description:
Sizes from the snapshot, so the history says what changed between
revisions without opening anything.

y_anchor.description: What the vertical axis is anchored to.

Role.description: What someone may do in a project, weakest first. Each role includes the ones before it: a `picker` writes their own picks, an `operator` also curates and replaces radargrams, and an `admin` also manages members and access.

RunningRender.description: One render holding a permit now.

target.description:
What it renders: a radargram's id, `draft N` for processing job
`N`'s draft, or `group G` or `catalog` for a merged level 2 export.

seconds.description: Since it took its render permit, in seconds.

waiting_for_radargram.description:
Whether it is still waiting for its radargram's lock, behind another
render of the same radargram, rather than rendering. Never for a
level 2 export, which takes no radargram's lock.

version.description:
The new version, also sent as the `ETag`. Send it as `If-Match` with
the next save.

warnings.description:
What the gprinterp validator noticed but did not refuse, such as a
feature without a stable id.

version.description: The new version, as the `ETag` gives it.
The new version, as the `ETag` gives it.

project_basemaps.description: The project's own basemaps, as `ridal.toml` holds them.

overlays.description: The project's vector overlays, as `ridal.toml` holds them.

size_bytes.description: The project's size on disk, in bytes.

max_bytes.description: The upload size limit, in bytes.

ScaleOption.description: One horizontal stretch factor the viewer offers.

text.description: The factor as text, without a trailing `.0`: `2`, `0.25`.

oneOf.description: Visible to everyone with viewing rights.
Visible only to its owner.

Scope.description: Who may see and edit a derived item.

SettingsUpdate.description:
The body of `PUT /api/v1/settings`. Every field is optional: absent
leaves the setting alone, and `null` clears it, restoring the built-in
default.

default_profile.description: The profile to use when a request names none.

default_xscale.description: Horizontal stretch to open radargrams at. Clearing it restores 1x.

hidden_profiles.description:
Built-in render profiles to leave out of the lists people choose
from (#183). An empty array hides none. The project's default cannot
be hidden.

personal_profiles.description:
Whether people may keep render profiles of their own (#183).
Turning it off keeps the ones they have, unused, until it is turned
on again.

basemaps.description:
The project's own basemaps, in the order the layer control should
list them (#177). An empty array removes them all.

default_basemap.description:
Which basemap someone who has not chosen sees. Clearing it means the
first offered.

built_in_basemap.description: Whether Ridal's built-in basemap is offered.

default_spacing.description:
The point spacing the layer-point download dialogs open on (#166).
Clearing it restores automatic spacing.

default_format.description: The format they open on. Clearing it restores WGS84 GeoJSON.

default_show_group_radargrams.description:
Whether the catalog opens with each group's radargrams listed
(#314). Clearing it restores shown.

oneOf.description:
Which groups' maps the catalog opens with shown (#447). Clearing it
restores every group's.

overlays.description:
The project's vector overlays (#177). An empty array removes them
all.

max_bytes.description:
The project's upload size limit in bytes (#173). Changing it needs
`admin`.

description.description:
The project's short description (#285); an empty string clears it
too. Changing it needs `admin`: it is read by every member and is the
project's public face.

Severity.description: How much the carried view can be trusted, worst first when reported.

ShapeChange.description: How the two revisions' grids compare.

SignedIn.description:
The response to signing in, by password (`POST /api/v1/auth/login`) or
by redeeming an invite (`POST /api/v1/auth/invite`). The session itself
is the `ridal_session` cookie set alongside it.

signed_out.description:
Always `true`. Signing out clears the cookie whether or not there
was a session.

SiteInfo.description: `GET /api/v1/site`: the site, and who the caller is in it.

accounts_configured.description: Whether the site has accounts to sign in to.

invite_ttl_days.description: How long an invite link is good for.

min_password_len.description: The shortest password an account may set.

theme.description: `light`, `dark`, or absent/`null`/empty to follow the device.

id.description: The conceptual radargram; stable across reprocessing.

revision_id.description: The specific processed revision; changes on every reprocess.

recordings.description:
The recordings, in merge order, each the files it is made of by name
and hash, as `POST /api/v1/raw` answered. Which file is the header,
the data and the positions is read from the names.

crs.description:
An EPSG code, such as `EPSG:32633`. Without it, the positions go in
the UTM zone that suits them best.

dem.description: One of the project's DEMs, by id (`GET /api/v1/dems`).

antenna_mhz.description: The antenna's frequency in MHz, overriding what the files say.

antenna_separation.description: The antenna separation in m, overriding what the files say.

oneOf.description:
What to call the radargram until it is served (#382 phase 7).
Absent keeps what the source had; `null` removes it.

SourceDem.description:
A source's link to one of the project's [`Dem`]s: which, and its file
when the link was made. A DEM's file cannot change while anything links
to it, so the two agree.

radargram_ids.description:
Sorted. Served or not: raw data uploaded for a radargram that has
not been processed yet is listed too.

names.description:
The names each source gives its radargram until it is served, for
those that give any (#382 phase 7).

SourceNames.description: The names a source gives a radargram that is not served yet.

SourceTransform.description: What is done to each sample before anything is resampled.

recordings.description:
What each recording's header and positions say, in merge order.
Only `PUT` reads the recordings; `GET` leaves this empty.

Split.description:
Why an output of a merging batch starts a new radargram instead of
continuing the one before it, in time order (#382 phase 2).

gap_seconds.description: From the end of the previous output to the start of this one.

over_threshold.description: Whether the gap alone is more than `--merge` allows.

incompatible.description:
Why the two cannot be one radargram, when they cannot: the first
thing `GPR::merge` refused.

manual.description:
Whether a person asked for a new radargram here, in the ingest
planner (#382); never in `batch-process`.

Staged.description:
`POST /api/v1/datasets/{radargram_id}/replace`: the file is staged, and
this is what committing it would do.

token.description:
Commits or discards the staged file, in
`/api/v1/datasets/{radargram_id}/replace/{token}`. Swept after 6 hours.

bytes.description: The size of the staged file.

StoredFile.description: `POST /api/v1/raw`: the file was stored, or was already.

x.description: Value in the anchor axis' unit.

TokenInfo.description: A stored API token, without its secret or its hash.

account.description: The account the token acts as.

grants.description: The projects the token may act in, and its ceiling in each.

expires.description: RFC 3339, or `null` for a token that never expires.

TokenSummary.description: An API token as its holder may see it: never its secret (#194).

id.description: Names the token in lists and the audit log, and revokes it.

grants.description:
The projects the token may act in, and its ceiling in each. In each,
the account's own membership also applies.

expires.description: RFC 3339, or `null` for a token that never expires.

TopoDiagnostics.description: How trustworthy the elevation is, for warning about a suspect one.

TopoGeometry.description:
`GET /api/v1/datasets/{radargram_id}/views/topo/geometry`: how the
topographically corrected view is laid out.

dz.description: The vertical size of one row of the corrected view, in metres.

elevation_top.description: The elevation of its top row, in metres.

source_height.description: Rows in the radargram, and in the corrected view.

shift.description:
Per-trace downward shift, in samples. ~90 KB of JSON on the largest
file in the test corpus, which is not a cheaper form to send: the
client needs the per-trace shift regardless, to place and cull picks
in the corrected view (#168), and it compresses well.

fingerprint.description:
A stable identifier of this resolved geometry, carried by the
frontend as a chunk-URL query parameter so an elevation-range edit
(which keeps the same view/x/y/profile) busts the browser's own
image cache instead of being served a stale chunk. The server does
not read this back on a chunk request -- the current override is
always the source of truth for what a chunk renders.

TopoRange.description:
The elevation range the corrected view is limited to, in metres. `null`
on a side that is not limited.

amplitude.description: One value per sample, top down.

Track.description: A radargram's track, simplified for drawing on a map.

TrackSegment.description:
One continuous stretch of a track. A gap between segments is a real gap
in the survey, such as a standstill.

trace_start.description: The first and last trace it covers.

length_m.description: Its length along the ground, in metres.

TrackVertex.description: One vertex of a simplified track, in WGS84.

Unit.description: The unit an expression is written in.

UnreadableInterpretation.description: A stored interpretation that could not be summarized.

path.description: The file or directory, relative to `interpretations/`.

UpdateMemberBody.description:
The body of `PUT /api/v1/projects/{key}/members/{name}`. A field left
out is not changed.

name.description: The new display name; `null` or empty removes it.

UploadStatus.description: An upload, and how far it has got.

size.description: The whole file's size in bytes, as declared.

offset.description:
How many bytes have arrived: where the next chunk starts. Equal to
`size` once the upload can be used.

expires_at.description: When the upload is deleted if nothing more is sent to it, RFC 3339.
